thread:
Alex Chen: Quick q — I switched from contractor to full-time. My Redwood health starts 2024-04-01, but I had medical visits Jan–Mar under my previous employer plan. Will those expenses count toward the new plan's deductible/OOP? Want to avoid paying twice. @Maya - People Ops tagging you for help. Thanks!

Maya - People Ops: Hey Alex — short answer: usually deductibles don't automatically transfer between employers. But some carriers offer a 'deductible credit' if you provide EOBs or claim summaries from the prior plan. Which carrier was your previous plan through?

Alex Chen: Previous was through Aurelia Health (employer plan). New carrier is also Aurelia Health through Redwood — same carrier! :eyes:

Maya - People Ops: ahhh ok that helps. If it's the same carrier they often can apply prior-plan deductible credits. You'll need EOBs or claim explanation pages with dates and amounts. Please upload them to the Benefits Portal (Benefits > Documents > Upload) and select "Previous Coverage Credit". Note: deadline is 90 days from your coverage effective date. I can open an internal submission once uploaded.

Alex Chen: Uploaded the PDF: alex_2024-eobs.pdf (contains three EOBs). I also asked Aurelia and they replied we need to submit a form.

Benefits Bot: Enrollment change processed for Alex Chen — new coverage effective 2024-04-01. Reminder: Claim credit requests require prior-plan EOBs + carrier form. Submit via Benefits Portal -> Submit 'Previous Coverage Credit' form. Details: https://benefits.redwood.com/claims-credit

Maya - People Ops: Thanks — I'll kick off an internal submission to Aurelia and attach Alex's docs. @Insurance Ops can you confirm whether we should also fill out Aurelia's carrier-specific 'Deductible Credit Request' or if portal upload is sufficient?

Insurance Ops: We should do both: portal upload plus carrier-specific form entry. I can complete the carrier portal entry but I need the EOB patient account numbers (if present) and the claim dates. If any EOBs have redacted identifiers, that's OK. Typical carrier turnaround is ~2–6 weeks. If the credit is denied, People Ops will help file an appeal. Tag me and I'll push it through.

Ross Patel: FYI from finance: if the carrier approves credit and it reduces your deductible retroactively, we can request an adjustment/refund for any amounts you already paid under the new plan. Send me the claim IDs and payment receipts and I'll coordinate with billing.

Alex Chen: Great — thanks everyone. @Maya please DM me next steps once submitted. :thumbsup:

Maya - People Ops: Will do. Also quick reminder: please don't post SSNs or sensitive IDs in channel. Use the portal upload or DM for redacted copies.
